text:
maria: quick heads-up — bringing up hf://open-artefact/gpt-lite-1 on RW and hit a weird sampling collapse when using quantized int8 + our default gen param mapping.

simon: what do you mean by collapse? low diversity? repeated tokens?

maria: repeated short loops. example: temperature 0.8 in HF -> our mapping coerced it to "0.8" (string) in genconfig during import, sampler ended up using default 0.0. output was deterministic.

kai: omg the string coercion again. where in the pipeline? hf->generation_config.json loader?

maria: yes, loader in model-onboarding service. code expects numbers but HF sometimes serializes as strings in legacy checkpoints. we have a fallback but it only normalizes top_k/top_p, missed temperature for some models.

ryan: also pay attention to rep_penalty interplay with top_p. if rep_penalty > 1 and top_p small, beam-like behavior emerges on quantized kernels. noticed that in local int8 experiments.

maria: exactly. int8 sampling implementation uses a different logit adjustment path. rep_penalty gets applied after quant truncation which amplifies token stickiness. result: repeats.

eva: do we have a reproducible snippet?

maria: paste from test harness:
```json
{
  "generation_config.json": {
    "temperature": "0.8",
    "top_p": 0.92,
    "top_k": 50,
    "repetition_penalty": 1.1
  }
}
```

maria: after import -> Redwood default layer becomes:
```json
{
  "temperature": 0.0,  // dropped due to string parse fail
  "top_p": 0.92,
  "top_k": 50,
  "repetition_penalty": 1.1
}
```

simon: ugh. That explains deterministic outputs. we should add strict validation and normalization during HF imports.

kai: +1. We also need a quick mitigation: if quantized runtime detected, clamp rep_penalty to [0.9,1.05] or warn in console.

ryan: beware clamping though — some model families legitimately require rep_penalty=1.2 for quality. Maybe runtime should switch to float emulation path for sampling when rep_penalty != 1.0.

maria: good point. proposal: two changes — 1) importer normalizes numeric strings to numbers and logs any coercions; 2) runtime checks quantization + rep_penalty interaction and emits a high-priority warning + opt-in float-safe sampling mode.

eva: can we add an eval harness to catch this class of regression? e.g., run a small prompt suite with sampling metrics: distinct-n, repetition-rate, median length under different quant/params.

maria: yep created a quick test set (short stories + QAs) and baseline metrics for fp16, int8, and our RK-sampling. When importer fails to coerce temperature, distinct-1 drops ~35% in int8.

simon: file a ticket?

maria: filed RW-1342. summary in the ticket: "HF import numeric coercion + quantized sampling order-of-ops causes rep_penalty-induced repetition". Assigned to @kai and @ryan for runtime mitigation and to @eva for eval harness.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: onboarding-service@staging -> v0.51.3 (changes: generation_config parsing fix) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kai: I'll own the coercion patch and add schema validation + unit tests. quick patch: use jsonschema with types: ["number","integer"] and coerceNumbers flag.

ryan: I'll prototype float-emulation sampling mode that runs sampling logits in fp32 when rep_penalty != 1.0. perf impact should be small for low-throughput evals.

eva: I'll wire the eval harness into CI and add a regression threshold: if distinct-1 down > 10% vs baseline for a quantized config, fail onboarding.

maria: thanks team. next steps: patch importer (kai), runtime safe-sample (ryan), eval in CI (eva). we should also add a docs note: "HF generation_config may have numeric strings; importer will coerce and log warnings".

simon: also add a quick support blurb for customers migrating HF checkpoints: check generation_config.json types and chat templates special tokens (sometimes templates reference 0 vs "0" token ids which trips tokenizer).

maria: yep. adding to RW migration checklist.

kai: will push a draft PR in ~2hrs.

ryan: i'll run manual int8 sanity tests after your patch lands.

eva: putting the eval tickets in CI tonight.

maria: awesome. closing loop once PRs merged. :thumbsup:
